item.title: Decode One Instruction: JE rel32
item.description:
Challenge: At address 0x140001008 (Windows x86-64), the raw bytes are 0F 84 12 34 00 00. Decode this instruction: name it, state its operand encoding, and compute the branch target address it jumps to.
Answer: je 0x140004420 (aka jz) - near conditional jump, rel32 form. 0F 84 is the two-byte opcode for JE/JZ rel32; the 0F escape distinguishes the near (32-bit displacement) conditional jumps from the short form (single-byte opcode 0x74, 8-bit displacement), needed when the target is too far for a signed 8-bit offset. The remaining bytes 12 34 00 00 are the little-endian signed displacement 0x00003412 = 13330. Displacements are relative to the next instruction: 0x140001008 + 6 (instruction length) = 0x14000100E, so target = 0x14000100E + 0x3412 = 0x140004420.
